newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's cabinet sacks energy company board.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's cabinet sacks energy company board.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim government has fired the board of directors of the National Electricity Company (NEC) and postponed a price increase proposed by the sacked board, the interim prime minister said on Thursday.
"The reason is that the management has not supported its proposal for electricity and heating price hikes from April 1 with reasonable cost analysis," Stefan Sofianski told reporters.
The new members were not named.

The cabinet has postponed the increase of power prices from April 1 "due to a lack of a development and restructuring programme of the sector and unclear structure of spendings and cost of the production", he said.
The cabinet will discuss price rises at its meeting on Monday.
"The new (power) price rises should be the last until June, when a currency board should be implemented," Sofianski said.

Bulgaria's authorities have agreed to a tough programme of restructuring, privatisation and budget discipline, including implementation of a fixed exchange rate system, called a currency board, to help stabilise the crumbling economy and repay foreign debts.
NEC has proposed a 30 percent increase of the electricity prices and a 70 percent rise of central heating prices.
The cabinet has also decided that the NEC, which produces 87 percent of Bulgaria's power, will be under the control of the government, not the Energy Ministry.
Since last July, energy prices have been revised each month, mainly according to the inflation rate and the lev/dollar exchange rate.
